newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power rises on PJM line limits. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power rises on PJM line limits. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]

text.p: Day-ahead prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic bulk electricity market rose Thursday, extending Wednesday's gains prompted by transmission limits in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool.
High demand for power from the western half of the grid and the refueling outage of the Limerick 2 nuclear unit divided the PJM system for a second day, market sources said.
Without the Limerick unit, utilities in eastern PJM must switch on more expensive oil and natural gas power plants to bring cheaper, coal-fired generation from the west.

Dispatch rate in the eastern half of PJM slipped to $25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from $26.50 Wednesday. The production cost in western PJM climbed to $17.00 from Wednesday's $16.25, market sources said.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Friday (excluding transmission costs) was traded at $24.25-$26.00/MWh, up from $24.00-$25.50 Wednesday.
PJM power prices for firm, off-peak (corrects from peak) delivery Friday held in the $16.00-$17.00 range.

Forecasts indicated PJM will enjoy mild weather through Friday with readings running five to eight degrees F above normal. Temperatures will cool to near normal levels this weekend before climbing again Monday.
PJM firm, peak electricity for delivery next week fell to $27.00-$28.00 from Wednesday's $28.00-30.00. Revised forecasts showed temperatures in PJM averaging normal to above normal most of next week.
PJM power for the rest of February fell $1.00-$1.50 to $27.50-$28.00 after Wednesday's jump.
March PJM deliveries tightened to $24.20-$24.30 from $24.10-24.45 Wednesday.
PJM prices for April and May firmed to $22.00-$22.20 from Wednesday's $21.95-22.20. June PJM electricity continued to reside in a $24.90-25.15 range.
July/August PJM power edged down to $30.20-$30.40 from Wednesday's $30.25-30.45.
PJM third-quarter electricity held at $27.90-28.10, and fourth-quarter PJM prices was steady at $23.85-24.00.
Firm, peak PJM deliveries for 1998 was quote near $25.95, the upper end of Wednesday's range.
Swing natural gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate remained at the $3.00 per million British thermal unit level (mmBtu) because of poor heating demand in the region.
As of 1252 EST, NYMEX March Henry Hub gas futures tumbled 9.0 cents to $2.340/mmBtu, extending Wednesday's loss on weak cash prices and mostly-mild U.S. weather this week.
